findings.title: Dry runs can write through copied symlinks
findings.description: `verbatimSymlinks: true` preserves absolute links into the real project or shared directories. The sandbox installer then follows those links through `mkdirSync`, `writeFileSync`, and pruning. For example, an absolute `.claude/rules` symlink lets `--dry-run` create rules outside the sandbox. Materialize isolated copies or reject escaping symlinks, and add a regression test verifying the linked directory remains unchanged.

findings.title: Native pruning lacks the removed containment checks
findings.description: The newly wired native installer trusts manifest paths and deletes matching files without checking lexical or real-path containment. A checksum-valid `../outside.md` entry—or a stale path beneath a symlinked directory—can delete files outside the checkout. The removed worktree pruner explicitly guarded both cases. Restore those protections in the native manifest implementation and retain corresponding safety tests.

findings.title: Aborted dry runs discard their diagnostic output
findings.description: Buffered output is replayed only after `install()` returns successfully. If it throws `InstallAbort`, diagnostics such as missing rules directories or broken managed markers disappear; `installIde()` returns exit 1 without printing the exception. Replay buffered warnings and errors on failure before cleanup. Extend the existing abort test to assert that the underlying diagnostic reaches the caller.
